title: How a wake encounter became a fin separation
note: CHAIN AS THE NTSB ADOPTED IT ON 26 OCT 2004 · CONTRIBUTING FACTORS ORDERED BY A THREE-TO-TWO BOARD VOTE · THE PILOTS' UNION AND THE FIRST OFFICER'S FAMILY CONTESTED THE CAUSE

nodes.label: Second wake encounter, 09:15:51
nodes.sub: JAL47 heavy 1 min 40 s ahead · ~2,430 ft above ground

nodes.label: Wheel 64° right, then right pedal 1.7 in
AAMP training: rudder taught as roll control
A300-600 rudder: 32 lb and 1.2 in to full travel at 250 kt
nodes.sub: Finding 11 · lightest pedal forces of the transports evaluated

nodes.label: Inputs stop?
nodes.sub: NTSB: stopping at any time before 09:15:58.4 would have prevented the accident

nodes.label: Sideslip 11–12° · fin loads about twice the limit, beyond ultimate
Right rear lug fractures · fin separates
nodes.sub: 09:15:58.4 · ~251 kt · loud bang on the CVR at 09:15:58.5

_facts: CLAIMS-american587.md §B.6 probable cause verbatim (separation from loads beyond ultimate created by the first officer's unnecessary and excessive rudder pedal inputs; contributing: A300-600 rudder system design characteristics and elements of AAMP), fn 211 3–2 vote (c140), adopted 2004-10-26 (c139). ANCHORS: c18 1 min 40 s; c31/c32 second encounter 0915:51 ~2,430 ft agl; c33 wheel 64° R 0915:51.5; c34 pedal 1.7 in R 0915:51.9; c35 sequence; c39 rudder 10–11° R / sideslip 11–12° R at 0915:58.4; c41 fracture 0915:58.4; c42 bang 0915:58.5; c43 ~251 kt; c83 32 lb / 1.2 in at 250 KCAS; c94 ~2× limit, > ultimate (Finding 6); c106 Jan 1 1997 booklet. Findings 5, 8, 9, 11, 12 quoted from CLAIMS §B.6; the 'stopped making inputs at any time' sentence is the NTSB press release of Oct 26 2004 (CLAIMS §B.5). The note line records that the pilots' union (APA, 'aircraft-pilot coupling' submission, CLAIMS §B.6) and the first officer's family (Stan Molin, d. 2014, CLAIMS §C.4) contested the cause, per the attributed-never-asserted rule. 'Full-rudder' = the pedal travel (1.7–2.4 in) exceeded the 1.2 in needed for full rudder at 250 KCAS (c83); the pedals themselves did not reach their 4-in stop (c81).
